then.text: The Crescent in the rain. Still grand. Still cold. Now also damp.
Sun on the Crescent! Practically Bath. Don't tell Bath, it'll get ideas.

crescent_fan.text: That's the Crescent. Georgian, grand and very cold.
They built it to rival Bath. Bath hasn't noticed yet.

then.text: Raining and I'm filling bottles of water. I know. I KNOW. I can't stop.
Fog on the hills and steam off the well. Buxton looks like a spa from a storybook today.

well_filler.text: St Ann's Well. Twenty-eight degrees, all year round.
I've filled forty bottles. I'm not thirsty. I just can't stop.

opera_fan.text: The Opera House has the best acoustics in the Peaks.
I once sang the whole of Carmen. The pigeons applauded. Politely.

then.text: The ducks love this drizzle. They're having the best day of anyone in Buxton.
Morning! The ducks are already up and in charge. The sign is very clear.

duck_fan.text: {greeting} Pavilion Gardens. Ducks have right of way. It's on the sign.
I've tried arguing. The ducks don't read.

then.text: Fog in the Goyt Valley today. Lovely and spooky, but stick to the path, eh.
Grand day for the Goyt! You can see half of Derbyshire from the top.

goyt_guide.text: That gap leads up into the Goyt Valley. It's the old packhorse road to Manchester.
Salt and silk went one way, cotton the other. Nowadays it's mostly walkers and the odd lost sat-nav.
Wrap up. Manchester is thirty miles north and, I'm told, wetter.

sheffield_warden.text: The road to Sheffield's closed for resurfacing. Come back when you've seen a bit more of the country.
